memories.content: Link expected participant burden in each user study task to its corresponding mitigation strategy.
Specify the accommodations necessary for participants to access the prototype and research tasks.
Specify how accessibility accommodations will be provided during user study sessions.
Describe how personal identifiers will be separated from research data immediately after collection.
Specify the equipment to be loaned to participants who lack necessary devices.
Describe the procedure for returning equipment loaned to participants.
HCI ethics reviewers verify that expected burdens and mitigation strategies correspond to each user study task.
Inform participants that the formative evaluation prototype is not a finished service.
Set an upper limit on cumulative task burden when requesting repeated evaluations from the same participant.
The author of this proposal tends to emphasize expected benefits of the prototype over participant burden.
In organizations where leaders or institutional staff handle recruitment, recruitment authority and academic or professional evaluation authority may be combined in the same role.
Do not change names referring to the same user roles, system functions, or operational stages midway.
Use abbreviations only for long recurring terms in a two-page proposal.
Present the full term and abbreviation together when using an abbreviation for the first time.
Refer to participants based on the roles they perform in the study rather than their status.
Reviewers from different subfields find it difficult to infer an abbreviation from context alone when it is not defined at first use.
When introducing an operational role for the first time, define both the decisions it can make and the actions it performs.
Individuals holding identical job titles may possess different system modification privileges and data access rights depending on their deployment site.
The user tends to group distinct field roles under the single label “user.”

analysis.overview: The frames address complementary but operationally separate concerns. The reference frame concentrates on participant protection, access, equipment, privacy, and recruitment ethics, while the compared frame concentrates on terminology, abbreviations, and precise role definitions. No scope-aligned overlap or contradiction is established.

relations.reason: These memories state complementary authoring and review aspects of one reference-only requirement for task-level burden-to-mitigation correspondence.
relations.summary: Expected participant burdens and mitigation strategies are linked task by task and verified during ethics review.

relations.reason: These memories split one reference-only accommodation plan into identifying access needs and explaining operational provision.
relations.summary: Necessary accessibility accommodations and the way they will be delivered during sessions must be specified.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful reference-only privacy procedure with no operational counterpart in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Personal identifiers must be separated from research data immediately after collection.

relations.reason: These memories describe the provision and return components of one reference-only equipment-lending process.
relations.summary: Participant equipment lending must identify the devices supplied and the procedure for returning them.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful reference-only disclosure requirement absent from the compared frame.
relations.summary: Participants must be told that the formative evaluation prototype is not a finished service.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful reference-only safeguard for repeat participation.
relations.summary: Repeated evaluations involving the same participant require an upper limit on cumulative task burden.

relations.reason: This reference-only observation identifies a specific framing tendency rather than a terminology or role-definition policy.
relations.summary: The proposal author tends to emphasize anticipated prototype benefits over participant burden.

relations.reason: This is a reference-only organizational ethics condition concerning potentially combined authority, not a general rule for documenting operational roles.
relations.summary: In institution-led recruitment, one role may combine recruitment authority with academic or professional evaluation authority.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful compared-only terminology rule.
relations.summary: Names for the same roles, system functions, and operational stages should remain consistent throughout the proposal.

relations.reason: These memories state the scope, required introduction, and reviewer-centered rationale of one compared-only abbreviation policy.
relations.summary: A short proposal should reserve abbreviations for long recurring terms and define each abbreviation at first use because reviewers may not infer it reliably.

relations.reason: These memories express one compared-only role-labeling principle and identify the tendency it is intended to correct.
relations.summary: Participants should be labeled by their study roles, with distinct field roles kept separate rather than collapsed under status labels or “user.”

relations.reason: These memories combine a compared-only role-definition rule with the deployment-specific condition that makes title-based definitions insufficient.
relations.summary: Operational roles should be defined through their decisions and actions because identical titles may carry different modification privileges and data access across sites.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame covers consistent terminology, restrained and defined abbreviations, role-based participant labels, and defining operational roles through actual decisions, actions, privileges, and access.
reports.reference_only: The reference frame covers task-level burden mitigation, accommodations, data separation, equipment lending, prototype disclosure, cumulative burden, benefit-burden framing, and recruitment authority risks.
